newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to up again, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to up again, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to slightly higher Friday in sluggish trade, with firmer crude and gas prices and forecasts for colder Northeast weather next week still underpinning the complex.
"There's not much demand but sellers backed off when they saw crude (rally)," said one cash trader, noting more cool Northeast weather next week could prop up the market.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained a quarter to about $15.25-50 a barrel, with April one percent paper up about 50 cents to $15.75-16.00 on firmer crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally held steady at $18.25-50 and $16.75, respectively.
High sulphurs in New York notionally were unchanged to up slightly.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was 25 cents higher at $14.00-25, while three percent notionally firmed 25-50 cents to $13.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

On Friday, prospects for colder Northeast weather again firmed New York city gate swing gas prices slightly to about $2.30/mmBtu, or about $14.49 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was little changed in the $1.97/mmBtu area, or $12.41 a barrel.
